With 10 per cent or less of the total, one cannot threaten the political position of the majority while simultaneously the minority functions as an ornament and can even serve as proof of the will to create a 'multi-ethnic society.'" Now, that was Mr. Pogarcic's view at the time as stated in this article. Was that view held by a number of the other people that we just looked at a few moments ago who were members of the presidential council and the other Herceg-Bosna HVO leadership at the time?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This certainly wasn't the opinion of the other members. I would like to point out that Pogarcic actually said that he believed that the Dayton Accords were acceptable for the Croats, and then he continued to provide his own opinion with which I personally and some other people in the council would certainly not agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Would you agree, sir, that with the statement in this document that all three of the ethnic parties --

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Apologise. Your Honour -- Your Honours, I apologise. I would like to react at this point because the Prosecutor ties this statement -- we don't know whether this is a statement or not. We don't know how credible the article actually is -- with Mr. Pogarcic's statement as a member of the presidential council, and then he ties that to the opinions of the other members of the presidential council, assuming that the opinion was the same as the opinion of their secretary. Mr. Pogarcic provided a statement as the deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs of the republic and federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Maybe it would be more correct to ask the witness whether the entire Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Bosnia-Herzegovina held the same opinion, because that was the gentleman's position at the time, which is clearly visible from the title of the article in the Croatian version. And I can't even see the date. I don't know when this was. It was in December 1995, which was much later than his appointment in the presidential council. It is even disputable whether he was still the secretary of that council, whether that council was still operational at the time when he provided this interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Your observation is on the transcript. We have to finish in a few minutes and I have some advice to give to the witness. I would like the registrar to tell me exactly how much time has been used up so far by the Prosecution. The Prosecution so far with all these objections only used five hours and 50 minutes. It still has 2 hours and 10 minutes left. Witness, you are the witness of justice now. You have made the solemn declaration. You are under oath. You can no longer contact Mr. Karnavas throughout the entire time between your -- now and your new testimony. Mr. Karnavas must not call you. If we hear about this, you know, this would really create a big problem. You are now almost finished with the cross-examination. Of course you're not supposed to contact Mr. Scott either. You can go back to your own business, but please do not mention your testimony so far. Please make sure that with the -- to go to the -- to the witness section to ask them for a plane ticket so you can come back on November 17th. The Prosecution will have two hours and ten minutes for the cross-examination so normally it should wrap up its cross-examination on the Monday when we resume with your testimony hoping that we won't run into any dramas or objections, lengthy objections. The next day Mr. Karnavas told us that he would need at least two hours, maybe less, for additional questions and then that will be -- and then you will be done with your testimony. You were one of the very important witnesses in this case not only for the Prlic Defence, especially in terms of the time required for your examination, so we will have the pleasure of seeing you again in a few weeks. We will now -- we'll be hearing the witness schedule for next week. You have set aside four hours for this witness, Mr. Karnavas, is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I did. We will try to be -- to get it under four, but we've asked for four, but I do not suspect it's going to go over four, but we are -- we are expecting the witness to come in on time, and he was prepared last time. We will have to re-prepare again, but we'll try to be as efficient as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It's true we've already seen him, and this -- for this witness it will also be a second time. It's almost 7.00. I wish everyone a pleasant evening, and we will meet again next Monday. I wish a safe return home to Mr. Tomic. Just for a while, unfortunately, but we will be very happy to see you again. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 10th day of November, 2008, at 2.15 p.m.
